hints: Focus on what mass number really counts, it is protons plus neutrons together, not just one of them.
Remember iron always has atomic number 26, so every iron atom has 26 protons.
Subtract the number of protons from the mass number of 60 to leave behind just the neutrons.
walkthrough:
**Recall what mass number means**

Mass number is the total number of particles in the nucleus. That is protons plus neutrons.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{mass number} = \text{protons} + \text{neutrons}$$

**Find the number of protons in iron**

The identity of an element tells you its protons. Iron, $\text{Fe}$, has proton number (atomic number) 26, so it has 26 protons.

**Calculate the neutrons**

Rearrange to find neutrons by subtraction.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{neutrons} = \text{mass number} - \text{protons} = 60 - 26 = 34$$

options.A: 26 is the proton number (atomic number) of iron, not the neutron count. Choosing this confuses protons with neutrons.
options.B: 30 is half of 60. There is no rule that protons and neutrons split equally, you must use the actual atomic number of iron, 26.
options.C: Correct and well done. Neutrons = 60 - 26 = 34. This correctly subtracts the 26 protons of iron from the mass number 60.
options.D: 60 is the mass number itself, the sum of protons plus neutrons. Choosing this forgets to subtract the protons.
